\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کارتخوان} (kârtkhân)}{کارتخوان (kârtkhân)}]{\fa{کارتخوان} (kârtkhân) — a card machine, a card reader}

\label{lesson:FA-C461-kartkhan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a fitting room, then the Persian for to like.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کارتخوان}}
\textbf{\fa{کارتخوان}} (\emph{kârtkhân}) — \textquotedblleft{}a card machine, a card reader\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کارتخوان} \fa{نانوایی} \fa{خراب} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kârtkhân-e nânvâyi kharâb bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bakery's card machine was out of order.
\end{quote}

\emph{kârt} 'card' + \emph{khân} 'reader', from \emph{khândan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kârtkhân} is built from \emph{kârt} 'card', which EtymDB takes from French \emph{carte}, and native \emph{khân}, the present stem of \emph{khândan} 'to read'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kârtkhân}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kârtkhân}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kârtkhân}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a fitting room, then the Persian for to like, then say \emph{kârtkhân} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کارت} \fa{به} \fa{کارت} \fa{کردن} (kârt-be-kârt kardan)}{کارت به کارت کردن (kârt-be-kârt kardan)}]{\fa{کارت} \fa{به} \fa{کارت} \fa{کردن} (kârt-be-kârt kardan) — to transfer money from card to card}

\label{lesson:FA-C461-kart-be-kart-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to like, then the Persian for a card machine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کارت} \fa{به} \fa{کارت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{کارت} \fa{به} \fa{کارت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{kârt-be-kârt kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to transfer money from card to card\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پول} \fa{بلیت} \fa{را} \fa{برای} \fa{دوستم} \fa{کارت} \fa{به} \fa{کارت} \fa{کردم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pul-e bilit râ barâ-ye dustam kârt-be-kârt kardam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I transferred the ticket money to my friend by card.
\end{quote}

Very common in Iran: money goes from one bank card to another by phone or cash machine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kârt-be-kârt kardan} is built from \emph{kârt} 'card', which EtymDB takes from French \emph{carte}, twice over with \emph{be} 'to', and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kârt-be-kârt kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kârt-be-kârt kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kârt-be-kârt kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to like, then the Persian for a card machine, then say \emph{kârt-be-kârt kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{کارت} \fa{به} \fa{کارت} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To transfer money from card to card\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{نسیه} (nesye)}{نسیه (nesye)}]{\fa{نسیه} (nesye) — on credit, on account (buying now and paying later)}

\label{lesson:FA-C461-nesye}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a card machine, then the Persian for to transfer money from card to card.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{نسیه}}
\textbf{\fa{نسیه}} (\emph{nesye}) — \textquotedblleft{}on credit, on account (buying now and paying later)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بقال} \fa{محله} \fa{به} \fa{ما} \fa{نسیه} \fa{میدهد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Baqqâl-e mahalle be mâ nesye midahad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The local grocer lets us buy on credit.
\end{quote}

\emph{Nesye kharidan} — to buy on credit. The opposite is \emph{naqd} 'cash'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{nesye} was borrowed from Arabic and is usually traced to Arabic \emph{nasīʾa} 'deferment, sale on credit'. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nesye}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{nesye}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a card machine, then the Persian for to transfer money from card to card, then say \emph{nesye} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پول} \fa{خرد} (pul-e khord)}{پول خرد (pul-e khord)}]{\fa{پول} \fa{خرد} (pul-e khord) — small change, coins}

\label{lesson:FA-C461-pul-e-khord}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to transfer money from card to card, then the Persian for on credit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پول} \fa{خرد}}
\textbf{\fa{پول} \fa{خرد}} (\emph{pul-e khord}) — \textquotedblleft{}small change, coins\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{راننده} \fa{تاکسی} \fa{پول} \fa{خرد} \fa{نداشت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Rânande-ye tâksi pul-e khord nadâsht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The taxi driver didn't have any change.
\end{quote}

\emph{pul} 'money' + \emph{khord} 'small'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pul-e khord} is built from \emph{pul} 'money', which EtymDB glosses 'change, small money', and native \emph{khord} 'small, broken', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{xward}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to transfer money from card to card, then the Persian for on credit, then say \emph{pul-e khord} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{صرافی} (sarrâfi)}{صرافی (sarrâfi)}]{\fa{صرافی} (sarrâfi) — a bureau de change, an exchange office}

\label{lesson:FA-C461-sarrafi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for on credit, then the Persian for small change.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{صرافی}}
\textbf{\fa{صرافی}} (\emph{sarrâfi}) — \textquotedblleft{}a bureau de change, an exchange office\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{صرافی} \fa{دلار} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{ریال} \fa{تبدیل} \fa{کردیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar sarrâfi dolâr râ be riyâl tabdil kardim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
At the exchange office we changed dollars into rials.
\end{quote}

The money changer is the \emph{sarrâf}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sarrâfi} is built from \emph{sarrâf} 'money changer', a loan usually traced to Arabic \emph{ṣarrāf}, and the Persian ending \emph{-i}. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
